Why Prosper businesses miss calls

Prosper has a median household income of about $195,000, the highest among the Texas cities we cover. One in three workers is in finance, real estate or professional services. New homes keep builders, pool companies and landscapers busy, while busy families expect fast replies. Competition for these customers is real, so a quick, polished answer on the first call can matter more than a low price.

Which Prosper businesses benefit most?

  • Real estate agents: New-home buyers call on evenings and weekends.
  • HVAC and contractors: New builds still need regular service.
  • Dental offices: Families can book outside school hours.

Can you keep your Prosper phone number?

Yes. Prosper callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
